g.textArea: Nobody types inventory in this workbook: every count is an XLOOKUP into the external _BC.xlsm file on SharePoint.

rect.data-description: LOOKUP (other sheet or table). Formula: =LET(no,Products[No.],grp,Products[Gen. Prod. Posting Group],ast,IFERROR(Products[Asset],""),keep,((grp="FG")+(grp="FG-DIST"))*(ast<>"Charges / Fees"),SORTBY(FILTER(no,keep),FILTER(grp,keep),1)). 275 FG packs then 120 FG-DIST cases. Same formula on every day sheet.
FORMULA (this sheet). Formula: =A3. Feeds: every lookup on the row, DSD_DSnD and Dist_DSnD SUMIFS/XLOOKUP key.
LOOKUP (other sheet or table). Formula: =XLOOKUP([@Code],Products[No.],Products[Description]).

LOOKUP (other sheet or table). Opening stock. Sunday only reads the external file: =XLOOKUP([@Code],'[1]Sunday - Inventory'!$A$4:$A$450,'[1]Sunday - Inventory'!$C$4:$C$450). Monday to Friday use the previous day's Final Inventory.
INPUT (typed). Blank on Sunday. Monday to Friday calculate it (see right). Nothing reads it.
FORMULA (this sheet). Count check: what the chain says we had against what was counted. Formula: =[@Initial Inventory]-([@Freezer]+[@Floor]). Display only.
LOOKUP (other sheet or table). Formula: =XLOOKUP([@Code],'[1]Sunday - Inventory'!$A$4:$A$450,'[1]Sunday - Inventory'!$F$4:$F$450). Column F of the external tab.
LOOKUP (other sheet or table). External column G, same XLOOKUP pattern.
LOOKUP (other sheet or table). External column H. Already promised, so subtracted from Total.
FORMULA (this sheet). Stock on hand. Formula: =[@Freezer]+[@Floor]-[@Late/Day Orders]-[@Inv. Discounts]. Feeds: DSD_DSnD S_Floor (SUMIFS), Dist_DSnD 0_/1_/2_Inventory when today is Sunday.
LOOKUP (other sheet or table). External column J: baked and wrapped today.
LOOKUP (other sheet or table). External column K: shipped today.
FORMULA (this sheet). Closing stock. Formula: =[@Total]+[@Wrapped]-[@Order]. Feeds: Monday Initial Inventory.
LOOKUP (other sheet or table). External column M. Subtracted from Total.
INPUT (typed). Notes, Temp, Weight, Color Lok, Bag Lot, New Bag Lot. Typed on the sheet, all blank, nothing reads them.
FORMULA (this sheet). Formula: =B$1-DATE(YEAR(B$1),1,1)+1. Uses the typed Sunday!B1 date.
FORMULA (this sheet). Monday!B1 =Sunday!B1+1; each later day adds one.
LOOKUP (other sheet or table). Formula: =XLOOKUP([@Code],Sunday[Code],Sunday[Final Inventory]). Tuesday reads Monday, and so on.
LOOKUP (other sheet or table). Formula: =XLOOKUP([@Code],Sunday[Code],Sunday[Freezer])-XLOOKUP([@Code],Sunday[Code],Sunday[Order]). Informational; nothing reads it.

rect.data-title: Counts (G, H, I, K, L, N)
rect.data-description: LOOKUP (other sheet or table). Same XLOOKUP as Sunday against that day's external tab: 'Monday - Inventory', 'Tuesday -Inventory', 'Wednesday - Inventory', 'Thursday - Inventory', 'Friday-Inventory'.
FORMULA (this sheet). Same formulas as Sunday.

NOTE. They turn the floor count into stock on hand (Total). Supply and Demand nets that against expected demand, Final Inventory rolls to the next morning, and Diferencias shows where the count and the chain disagree.
NOTE. Sunday Final 90,429 = Monday Initial 90,429, and so on through the week.
NOTE. Thursday is partly entered. Friday is not counted yet (Freezer, Floor, Total = 0), which is why Friday production is negative for most items.
NOTE. Sunday: Freezer 79, Order 27, Final 52. Monday: Initial 52, Freezer (Day Before) 79 - 27 = 52, Wrapped 96, Order 9, Final 139.
ISSUE. B1 = 2026-08-30 but the planning anchor is 2026-09-20. Julian dates print 242 to 247 instead of 263 to 268.

rect.data-title: Tables longer than their row list
rect.data-description: ISSUE. Tuesday +3 rows, Wednesday to Friday +52 rows of #N/A below the spill. Harmless for totals, but untidy (see Recon).

rect.data-title: SKUs missing from the external tabs
rect.data-description: ISSUE. F6214, F52550, F53220 (and F52540) are not on the _BC.xlsm tabs, so their counts return #N/A.
ISSUE. 'Tuesday -Inventory' and 'Friday-Inventory' break the 'Day - Inventory' pattern. Renaming a tab breaks the link.

rect.data-title: Everything depends on one linked file
rect.data-description: ISSUE. If _BC.xlsm moves or the link breaks, every day table and all distribution demand freeze at their last values.
ISSUE. Protection is defined but not switched on, so formula columns can be typed over.
